paras.zh: 这种先前未报道的纠缠是由这家研究公司首先发现的，该公司利用人工智能收集证据，专门从事世界各地的国家安全调查。这些联系可能会引发人们对黄爱丽在与首席执行官关系中的意图和行为的质疑，以及黄仁勋是否知道他的恋人与他的竞争对手密切相关。黄仁勋承认有外遇，但他与黄爱丽丝发生关系的确切时间尚不清楚。

paras.en: The mysterious saga of Alice Huang involves a tangle of interlocking corporations and transactions that show her connection to entities that ultimately provided computing power to Huawei in China.
paras.zh: 黄爱丽的神秘传奇涉及一系列相互关联的公司和交易，这些公司和交易显示了她与最终向华为在中国提供计算能力的实体的联系。

paras.en: Huawei is known as a Chinese government "state champion" in the technology and telecommunications sectors, meaning it receives enormous financial support from the government in Beijing so it can lower prices and undercut global competitors. It is considered a key part of the Chinese government's push for global technical dominance and is closely linked to the Chinese Communist Party.
paras.zh: 华为被称为中国政府在技术和电信领域的“国家冠军”，这意味着它获得了北京政府的巨额财政支持，因此可以降低价格并削弱全球竞争对手。它被认为是中国政府推动全球技术主导地位的关键部分，并与中国共产党密切相关。

paras.en: Businesses connected to Alice Huang were linked with supplying Nvidia computing power to Huawei, according to documents reviewed by CNBC, around the same time she and Jensen Huang were first publicly seen together in December 2023.
paras.zh: 根据 CNBC 查阅的文件，与 Alice Huang 有关的企业与向华为提供 Nvidia 计算能力有关，大约在同一时间，她和黄仁勋于 2023 年 12 月首次公开在一起。

paras.en: In 2024, Nvidia said Huawei was a top competitor, specifically in artificial intelligence chips including graphics processing units, central processing units and networking chips.
paras.zh: 2024年，英伟达表示华为是最大的竞争对手，特别是在人工智能芯片方面，包括图形处理单元、中央处理单元和网络芯片。

paras.en: "This activity, which surfaced through our analysis of Alice's network, warrants a national security and [technology] counterproliferation investigation," said Brian Andersen, Tesari's vice president for national security applications and a former supervisory special agent with Homeland Security Investigations.
paras.zh: Tesari 负责国家安全应用的副总裁、国土安全调查局前监督特工布莱恩·安德森 (Brian Andersen) 表示：“通过我们对 Alice 网络的分析发现的这一活动需要进行国家安全和[技术]反扩散调查。”

paras.en: If the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry Security and Homeland Security Investigations found evidence that anyone transferred "controlled equipment" to Huawei without authorization, potential charges might include include export-control violations, conspiracy and smuggling, Andersen said.
paras.zh: 安德森表示，如果美国商务部工业安全和国土安全调查局发现任何人未经授权向华为转让“受控设备”的证据，潜在的指控可能包括违反出口管制、共谋和走私。

paras.en: The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei is so convoluted that analysts at Tesari told CNBC that based on their previous investigative experience, they suspect it was designed to deliberately obscure the relationship.
paras.zh: Alice Huang 与华为之间的联系如此错综复杂，Tesari 的分析师告诉 CNBC，根据他们之前的调查经验，他们怀疑这是为了故意掩盖这种关系。

paras.en: Nvidia and Huawei did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment. Jensen Huang did not respond to a voicemail left on a mobile phone. Alice Huang could not be reached.
paras.zh: 英伟达和华为没有回应 CNBC 的置评请求。黄仁勋没有回复手机上留下的语音邮件。无法联系到 Alice Huang。

paras.en: According to Chinese corporate records and media reports compiled by Tesari and provided to CNBC, Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le and who according to documents at the time was based in Hong Kong, in 2019 sold a cloud business she owned called Osmanthus to a Chinese gaming company called 7Road. A subsidiary of 7Road, which was based in Singapore, was spun off as "Megaspeed" in 2023. Megaspeed would go on to become a key Nvidia customer, helping facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms, The Information reported Tuesday.
paras.zh: 根据 Tesari 整理并提供给 CNBC 的中国企业记录和媒体报道，Alice Huang（中文名字是黄乐，根据当时的文件显示，她居住在香港）于 2019 年将她拥有的名为 Osmanthus 的云业务出售给了一家名为第七大道的中国游戏公司。 7Road 总部位于新加坡的子公司于 2023 年被分拆为“Megaspeed”。据 The Information 周二报道，Megaspeed 将继续成为 Nvidia 的重要客户，帮助 Nvidia 芯片向中国公司出货至少 75 亿美元。

paras.en: As early as 2016, Alice Huang had also become a co-owner of a financial firm known as Shanghai Hexi, which heavily invests in tech and data centers.In 2021, Hexi in turn acquired 27 percent of a company called Shanghai Century Longteng, a data center developer, which Hexi held until 2024. That firm owned a controlling 50.1 percent stake in a data center facility called Shenzhen Yifeng Technology Co., Ltd. in mainland China.
paras.zh: 早在2016年，Alice Huang还成为一家名为上海河西的金融公司的共同所有者，该公司大力投资科技和数据中心。2021年，河西又收购了一家名为上海世纪龙腾的数据中心开发商公司27%的股份，河西一直持有该公司直至2024年。该公司控股中国大陆一家名为深圳市亿丰科技有限公司的数据中心设施50.1%的股权。

paras.en: The key customer of that data center was Huawei Cloud, the Shenzhen, China-based subsidiary of Huawei Technologies.
paras.zh: 该数据中心的主要客户是华为技术有限公司位于中国深圳的子公司华为云。

paras.en: In addition, Alice Huang's firm Hexi guaranteed the loans required to finance the Shenzhen data center, which did business with Huawei.
paras.zh: 此外，Alice Huang的公司Hexi为与华为有业务往来的深圳数据中心提供融资所需的贷款提供担保。

paras.en: Hexi did not immediately respond to a message via its LinkedIn page sent outside of normal business hours.
paras.zh: 河西没有立即回复在正常工作时间之外通过其 LinkedIn 页面发送的消息。

paras.en: CNBC translated corporate records and Chinese news articles in Mandarin that Tesari provided.
paras.zh: CNBC 将 Tesari 提供的公司记录和中国新闻文章翻译成普通话。

paras.en: It's not clear if the Shenzhen data center was able to acquire Nvidia GPUs, but its majority owner began purchasing the chips in 2023. That company is known as Zhejiang Century Huatong Group and is a business partner of Alice Huang's Hexi through their joint ownership of Century Longteng.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚深圳数据中心是否能够购买 Nvidia GPU，但其大股东于 2023 年开始购买这些芯片。该公司名为浙江世纪华通集团，通过共同拥有世纪龙腾，是 Alice Huang 的河西的业务合作伙伴。

paras.en: That made Alice Huang a part owner of a data center providing computing power to Huawei. And that was happening at around the same time the first known sightings came of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang in public together.
paras.zh: 这使得爱丽丝黄成为为华为提供计算能力的数据中心的部分所有者。大约在同一时间，人们第一次看到爱丽丝·黄和黄仁勋在公共场合在一起。

paras.en: And that raises the question of why Huawei, which has access to Chinese made chips, would need to rent computing power from an outside entity.
paras.zh: 这就提出了一个问题：为什么能够使用中国制造芯片的华为需要从外部实体租用计算能力。

paras.en: Hexi exited its stake in the data center development company in 2024, but individuals within Alice Huang's network are still connected to the Shenzhen data center. Her husband Kang Wei is a longtime business associate who founded Hexi, where Alice Huang previously held an executive role. In 2022, Kang became an executive of Century Longteng, which owns the controlling stake in the Shenzhen data center and he also attended the company's signing of the Huawei agreement.
paras.zh: Hexi 于 2024 年退出了其在数据中心开发公司的股份，但 Alice Huang 网络内的个人仍然连接到深圳数据中心。她的丈夫康伟是一位长期商业伙伴，创立了河西，黄爱丽此前曾在河西担任高管职务。 2022年，康成为世纪龙腾的高管，该公司拥有深圳数据中心的控股权，并出席了该公司与华为协议的签署。

articles.title: Trump says ‘we don’t need a deal with Iran’

paras.en: The U.S. should no longer seek a deal with Iran, President Donald Trump said Thursday as he directed Vice President JD Vance to instead focus his attention on corruption and crime in Democratic cities and states.
paras.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周四表示，美国不应再寻求与伊朗达成协议，并指示副总统万斯将注意力集中在民主党城市和州的腐败和犯罪问题上。

paras.en: "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.
paras.zh: “我们不需要与伊朗达成协议。那些日子早已过去了，”特朗普在《真相社会》的帖子中写道。

paras.en: "We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Trump wrote, referring to the Strait of Hormuz, a key chokepoint in the ongoing U.S.-Iran war.
paras.zh: “我们有他们的钱，数千亿美元，我们也有他们的海峡！”特朗普写道，提到霍尔木兹海峡，这是正在进行的美伊战争的一个关键咽喉要道。

paras.en: The announcement came just over a week after Republicans suffered huge losses in the midterm election. Vance and other Republicans have pinned those losses on the Iran war, which the U.S. and Israel started in late February.
paras.zh: 这一消息是在共和党在中期选举中遭受巨大损失后一周多发布的。万斯和其他共和党人将这些损失归咎于美国和以色列于二月底发动的伊朗战争。

paras.en: In the weeks leading up to Election Day, Trump repeatedly suggested the U.S. could resume launching military strikes, which have largely subsided as a tense stalemate has taken hold in the region.
paras.zh: 在选举日之前的几周内，特朗普多次建议美国可以恢复发动军事打击，但随着该地区紧张的僵局，军事打击已基本平息。

paras.en: The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday reported that Vance, who has led diplomatic efforts with Iran in prior months, was considering face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official.
paras.zh: 《华尔街日报》周三报道称，前几个月领导与伊朗外交努力的万斯正在考虑与伊朗高级安全官员进行面对面会谈。

paras.en: Stock futures declined following Trump's post.
paras.zh: 特朗普发表讲话后，股票期货下跌。

paras.en: The unpopular Iran war, which Trump and others in his administration said would be won in a matter of weeks, is now in its ninth month with no clear end in sight. The conflict region has driven up global energy prices, creating a ripple effect through the economy and exacerbating concerns about inflation and affordability that were paramount to voters in the midterms.
paras.zh: 特朗普和他的政府中的其他人表示，不受欢迎的伊朗战争将在几周内获胜，现在已经进入第九个月，而且还没有明显结束的迹象。冲突地区推高了全球能源价格，对经济产生了连锁反应，并加剧了对中期选举选民最关心的通胀和负担能力的担忧。

paras.en: Corruption emerged as another top issue that broke in Democrats' favor in the election. Trump's post Thursday morning attempts to flip the script, blaming Democratic-run areas for allowing corruption and crime to proliferate.
paras.zh: 腐败成为另一个在选举中对民主党有利的首要问题。特朗普周四早上的帖子试图翻转剧本，指责民主党控制的地区允许腐败和犯罪激增。

paras.en: "I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.," Trump wrote.
paras.zh: 特朗普写道：“我已要求副总统万斯将全部注意力集中在美国民主党统治的城市和州发生的大规模腐败和犯罪上。”

paras.en: "The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters. Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month," the president wrote. "Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity."
paras.zh: 总统写道：“明尼苏达州、加利福尼亚州、伊利诺伊州等蓝州都是经营不善、腐败的灾难。每个月都有数十亿美元被盗。” “我们的预算可以通过纠正这种大规模犯罪活动来迅速实现平衡。”

paras.en: "CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership's blood!" he added.
paras.zh: “腐败是民主党领导层的血液！”他补充道。

articles.title: Jensen Huang leaving Nvidia risks a ‘brain drain’ from the AI chipmaker

paras.en: Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia, one of the world’s most valuable companies and the single most integral player in the artificial intelligence boom, could change the course of the technology, experts say, leading to a potential “brain drain” at Nvidia if others decide to leave alongside Huang.
paras.zh: 专家表示，黄仁勋从英伟达辞职可能会改变该技术的发展方向，英伟达是全球最有价值的公司之一，也是人工智能热潮中最重要的参与者，如果其他人决定与黄仁勋一起离开，则可能导致英伟达出现“人才流失”。

paras.en: Huang resigned after admitting to having a relationship with a woman who is an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Further reporting by the New York Times suggests Huang may have had another affair with an unnamed Nvidia executive. He will be replaced in the interim by Nvidia’s current chief financial officer, Colette Kress, the company said in a statement.
paras.zh: 黄在承认与一名据称是中国情报人员的女性发生关系后辞职。 《纽约时报》的进一步报道表明，黄可能与一位未透露姓名的英伟达高管有过另一段恋情。该公司在一份声明中表示，他将暂时由英伟达现任首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)接替。

paras.en: The reason why Huang’s departure could prove so crucial lies in Nvidia’s unusual corporate structure and the central role Huang has had in its chip design and innovation pipeline since its founding. “[Huang] is intimately involved in almost every aspect of the company,” says Ryan Fedasiuk, senior fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation, who studies the intersection of technology and national security.
paras.zh: 黄仁勋的离职之所以如此重要，是因为英伟达不同寻常的公司结构以及黄仁勋自成立以来在其芯片设计和创新渠道中发挥的核心作用。 “[Huang] 密切参与了公司的几乎各个方面，”美国创新基金会高级研究员 Ryan Fedasiuk 表示，他研究技术与国家安全的交叉点。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Since co-founding Nvidia in 1993, Huang has been the figurehead of the firm. His trademark leather jackets and aptitude for diplomacy have made him a main character in the ongoing AI race, which was kick-started by OpenAI’s November 2022 release of ChatGPT. Nvidia provides almost all the major AI labs and a slew of private firms with semiconductor chips—graphics processing units, or GPUs—that make AI work.
paras.zh: 自 1993 年共同创立 Nvidia 以来，黄仁勋一直是该公司的名义领导人。他标志性的皮夹克和外交才能使他成为正在进行的人工智能竞赛的主角，这场竞赛是由 OpenAI 2022 年 11 月发布的 ChatGPT 启动的。 Nvidia 为几乎所有主要的人工智能实验室和众多私营公司提供了使人工智能发挥作用的半导体芯片（图形处理单元或 GPU）。

paras.en: Nvidia’s dominance in the industry stems from these GPUs, which the firm initially developed for rendering computer games. That capability made them ideal for AI because they were able to process multiple equations in parallel—something that is essential to making a game run smoothly. As a result, Nvidia had a decades-long head start over its competitors, such as AMD or Intel, which are only now catching up.
paras.zh: Nvidia 在该行业的主导地位源于这些 GPU，该公司最初开发这些 GPU 是为了渲染电脑游戏。这种能力使它们成为人工智能的理想选择，因为它们能够并行处理多个方程——这对于游戏顺利运行至关重要。结果，英伟达领先AMD或英特尔等竞争对手数十年，而后者现在才迎头赶上。

paras.en: And when people think of Nvidia, they think of Huang. He has an unusually hands-on management style, with more than 60 direct reports, making his departure particularly difficult to navigate.
paras.zh: 当人们想到英伟达时，他们就会想到黄仁勋。他有着异常亲力亲为的管理风格，拥有 60 多名直接下属，这使得他的离职特别难以应对。

paras.en: “We believe he is deeply involved in all strategic decision making,” wrote Rick Schafer and Trevor Bowers, researchers at the investment bank Oppenheimer & Co, in a note. “We see massive shoes to fill and no obvious successor. His departure presents a material, potentially thesis-changing event.”
paras.zh: “我们相信他深入参与了所有战略决策，”投资银行奥本海默公司的研究人员里克·谢弗和特雷弗·鲍尔斯在一份报告中写道。 “我们看到大量的空缺需要填补，但没有明显的继任者。他的离开是一个重大的、可能改变论点的事件。”

paras.en: But Nvidia isn’t a one-man engineering operation. It employs tens of thousands of people, including some of the world’s leading chip designers—that leads Fedasiuk to believe the company should be capable of sustaining its technical progress without Huang at the helm.
paras.zh: 但英伟达并不是一家单人工程公司。该公司拥有数万名员工，其中包括一些世界领先的芯片设计师，这让 Fedasiuk 相信，即使没有黄仁勋的掌舵，该公司也应该能够保持技术进步。

paras.en: But Huang didn’t just provide technical capabilities. He also acted as a “voice of sanity” for the Trump administration amid the competition with China, says Kristy Loke, a researcher on the geopolitics of AI at MATS (Machine Alignment, Transparency, and Security) Research, an AI think tank. Huang also vocally supported open models, which make their core components public, allowing researchers to see how the models are trained. Huang was “making the case that as a general-purpose technology, AI should spread instead of be bottled up and sold at a premium,” Loke says.
paras.zh: 但黄先生提供的不仅仅是技术能力。人工智能智库 MATS（机器对齐、透明度和安全）研究中心的人工智能地缘政治研究员 Kristy Loke 表示，在与中国的竞争中，他还为特朗普政府发出了“理智的声音”。黄还公开支持开放模型，将其核心组件公开，让研究人员能够看到模型是如何训练的。洛克说，黄仁勋“证明，作为一种通用技术，人工智能应该传播，而不是被封闭起来并高价出售”。

paras.en: Still, the distraction caused by Huang’s departure, rather than the loss of his personal technical expertise, could ultimately cause more damage, Fedasiuk says. “I don’t think it’s right to conceive of this as ‘if Jensen goes, then there goes a huge blow to the company’s technical capability,’” he says. His concern is that the scandal could materially harm Nvidia’s ability to operate business as usual.
paras.zh: 费达修克表示，尽管如此，黄的离开所造成的分心，而不是他个人技术专长的丧失，最终可能会造成更大的损失。 “我认为‘如果詹森离开，公司的技术能力就会受到巨大打击’这样的想法是不正确的，”他说。他担心这一丑闻可能会严重损害英伟达正常运营业务的能力。

paras.en: “The longer this drags on,” Fedasiuk says, “the more distracted the company will grow, and the less effort or attention it will be able to dedicate to the real difficult technical problems.”
paras.zh: “这种情况拖得越久，”费达修克说，“公司的发展就越容易分心，对真正困难的技术问题投入的精力或注意力就越少。”

paras.en: Those challenges include developing chips capable of processing ever larger AI models, finding ways to move information between processors without introducing bottlenecks and improving the enormous energy demands of modern AI systems.
paras.zh: 这些挑战包括开发能够处理更大人工智能模型的芯片、找到在处理器之间移动信息而不引入瓶颈的方法以及改善现代人工智能系统的巨大能源需求。

paras.en: Huang’s swift departure could mean that much of that work may continue unabated—though who replaces Huang in the long run, and whether they can act as such a totemic figure as he had, is yet to be seen. Another key unanswered question is whether Huang’s departure will be the only one.
paras.zh: 黄的迅速离开可能意味着大部分工作可能会继续下去，尽管从长远来看谁会取代黄，以及他们是否能像他那样成为图腾人物，还有待观察。另一个尚未解答的关键问题是黄的离开是否是唯一的一个。

paras.en: “We see risk that a Huang departure creates a brain drain situation at the AI giant, threatening Nvidia’s pace of innovation, a critical competitive advantage,” the Oppenheimer researchers wrote.
paras.zh: 奥本海默研究人员写道：“我们认为，黄仁勋的离开可能会导致这家人工智能巨头出现人才流失，从而威胁到英伟达的创新步伐，而这是一项关键的竞争优势。”

articles.title: AI is disrupting math. Is science next?

paras.en: In March—eons ago in the current pell-mell of artificial intelligence developments—theoretical physicist Matthew Schwartz gave an ominous message to his peers: AI is going to do lots of science, so watch out. Schwartz’s warning, delivered in a speech at the American Physical Society’s annual meeting, was not particularly well received. Many physicists in the audience reacted with a mix of skepticism and derision to the Harvard University professor’s forecast, which seemed, at the time, too alarmist and too optimistic about AI’s capabilities to be true.
paras.zh: 今年三月，在当前人工智能发展的混乱时期，理论物理学家马修·施瓦茨（Matthew Schwartz）向他的同行发出了一个不祥的信息：人工智能将做很多科学研究，所以要小心。施瓦茨在美国物理学会年会上的一次演讲中提出的警告并没有受到特别好评。观众中的许多物理学家对这位哈佛大学教授的预测抱有怀疑和嘲笑的态度，当时的预测似乎过于危言耸听，对人工智能的能力过于乐观，令人难以置信。

paras.en: Now such warnings seem quaint. In the months following Schwartz’s talk, scientists have watched with growing awe and unease as an astonishing series of AI-powered advances has sparked an existential crisis for their colleagues in math. In May models from the company OpenAI, guided by humans, disproved a long-standing conjecture posed by the legendary mathematician Paul Erdős. In August, amid eddies of controversy, AI models effectively solved the Navier-Stokes problem, which has been one of math’s biggest quandaries. And in October OpenAI released 722 AI-generated preprints on some 370 open problems, including a partial solution to the Riemann hypothesis.
paras.zh: 现在这样的警告似乎很奇怪。在施瓦茨演讲后的几个月里，科学家们越来越敬畏和不安地看着人工智能驱动的一系列惊人进步给他们的数学同事引发了生存危机。今年 5 月，OpenAI 公司的模型在人类指导下反驳了传奇数学家 Paul Erdős 提出的长期猜想。今年八月，在争议的漩涡中，人工智能模型有效地解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，该问题一直是数学界最大的难题之一。 10 月，OpenAI 发布了 722 个人工智能生成的预印本，涉及约 370 个开放问题，其中包括黎曼假设的部分解决方案。

paras.en: While mathematicians seem to be staring down a future where AI automates many elements of solving proofs, the picture for scientists is still rather murky.
paras.zh: 虽然数学家们似乎正在展望人工智能将解决证明的许多要素自动化的未来，但科学家们的前景仍然相当模糊。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Scientists now routinely use AIs for coding and increasingly tap it for analysis as well. As for truly novel results, “I can’t name a result that’s a deep insight into physics yet,” says Schwartz, who is also a consultant for Anthropic, the company behind the Claude family of AI models. “Is that a fundamental limit, or is it just that tools aren’t ready yet? I’m pretty sure it’s that the tools aren’t ready yet.”
paras.zh: 科学家现在经常使用人工智能进行编码，并越来越多地利用它进行分析。至于真正新颖的结果，“我还无法说出一个对物理学有深刻见解的结果，”施瓦茨说，他也是 Anthropic 公司的顾问，该公司是 Claude 系列人工智能模型背后的公司。 “这是一个根本性的限制，还是只是工具还没有准备好？我很确定是工具还没有准备好。”

paras.en: But the tools are improving at a breakneck pace—and theoretical physics, arguably the area closest to math, could be next. In late October OpenAI and Anthropic alike announced their independent progress on a thorny problem that underpins the math of the Standard Model of particle physics. That same month a separate assessment found the latest AI models were nearly flawless at solving research-level theoretical physics problems—minor-but-substantial puzzles that an expert might figure out in a day.
paras.zh: 但这些工具正在以极快的速度改进——理论物理学，可以说是最接近数学的领域，可能是下一个。 10 月下旬，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都宣布了他们在支撑粒子物理标准模型数学的棘手问题上取得的独立进展。同月，一项单独的评估发现，最新的人工智能模型在解决研究级理论物理问题方面几乎完美无缺，这些问题虽小但很重要，专家可能一天就能解决。

paras.en: Amid such tumult, researchers from across the sciences who spoke with Scientific American showed little consensus about what exactly AI will be able to do and how it should be used in their fields. But all agreed that science was on the cusp of massive change.
paras.zh: 在这样的喧嚣中，接受《科学美国人》采访的来自各个科学领域的研究人员对于人工智能到底能做什么以及如何在各自的领域中使用它几乎没有达成共识。但所有人都同意科学正处于巨大变革的风口浪尖。

paras.en: “Right now everyone is trying to figure out where AI is going to go, and scientists are not alone in that,” says Mark Histed, a neuroscientist at the National Institute of Mental Health. “There’s a lot of uncertainty.”
paras.zh: 美国国家心理健康研究所的神经科学家马克·希斯特德 (Mark Histed) 表示：“现在每个人都在试图弄清楚人工智能将走向何方，科学家并不孤单。” “有很多不确定性。”

paras.en: Four short years ago large language models (LLMs) were struggling to add two-digit numbers, so it was a major step forward when they became proficient enough to pass eighth-grade math tests. Unlike calculators, they had no hard-coded method of doing arithmetic. As their name suggests, LLMs are trained on text—getting them to do math was seen widely as somehow backward. Now the situation has flipped: the most popular and dominant AI models (which are all LLMs) tend to produce merely “good” prose but can churn out superhuman feats of quantitative reasoning. Their sudden ascent has shaken mathematics to its core, and its human practitioners are struggling to chart a path forward.
paras.zh: 短短四年前，大型语言模型 (LLM) 正在努力添加两位数的数字，因此当它们熟练到足以通过八年级数学测试时，这是向前迈出的一大步。与计算器不同，它们没有硬编码的算术方法。正如他们的名字所暗示的，法学硕士接受的是文本训练——让他们做数学被广泛认为在某种程度上是落后的。现在情况发生了转变：最流行和占主导地位的人工智能模型（都是法学硕士）往往只能产生“好的”散文，但可以创造出超人的定量推理壮举。它们的突然崛起动摇了数学的核心，人类实践者正在努力寻找前进的道路。

paras.en: But this staggering progress is only partially explained by ever improving models; the other half of the equation is the nature of math, where exact solutions exist. LLMs can also take advantage of proof verification software, such as Lean, a programming language that can logically codify and confirm a result is true (even if no one fully understands the underlying math). “In the sciences, we don’t have such a verifier,” says N. M. Anoop Krishnan, an engineer studying AI at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, who is skeptical that LLMs can produce similarly epochal autonomous discoveries in science.
paras.zh: 但这种惊人的进步只能部分地用不断改进的模型来解释。方程的另一半是数学的本质，存在精确的解。法学硕士还可以利用证明验证软件，例如 Lean，一种可以逻辑编码并确认结果真实性的编程语言（即使没有人完全理解底层数学）。印度德里理工学院研究人工智能的工程师 N. M. Anoop Krishnan 表示：“在科学领域，我们没有这样的验证者。”他对法学硕士能否在科学领域产生类似的划时代自主发现表示怀疑。

paras.en: Current models excel when they have access to plentiful, well-vetted data. Thanks to training on much of all digitized human scientific knowledge, they can now deliver authoritative-sounding explanations on any given topic. But that doesn’t necessarily mean they can replace human experts. Good scientists rely on subtleties that rarely appear in peer-reviewed literature, such as negative results and hard-won tacit knowledge—“intuitions that are developed in the [scientific] process,” Krishnan says. Moreover, LLMs often homogenize their responses, making them less useful for devising genuinely novel ideas for exploratory scientific work. Even if these problems were surmounted, there’s the pesky existence of a physical world against which to validate, Krishnan points out. Designing a material in silico is no substitute for synthesizing it in the real world.
paras.zh: 当前的模型在能够访问大量、经过严格审查的数据时表现出色。由于接受了大部分数字化人类科学知识的培训，他们现在可以就任何给定主题提供听起来权威的解释。但这并不一定意味着它们可以取代人类专家。优秀的科学家依赖于同行评审文献中很少出现的微妙之处，例如负面结果和来之不易的隐性知识——“在[科学]过程中发展起来的直觉，”克里希南说。此外，法学硕士的回答常常趋于同质化，这使得他们在为探索性科学工作设计真正新颖的想法时用处不大。克里希南指出，即使这些问题得到了克服，仍然需要验证物理世界的烦人存在。在计算机中设计材料并不能替代在现实世界中合成材料。

paras.en: Indeed, the ability to predict and design novel materials has historically been seen as one of AI’s greatest promises. Thus far, however, there’s been little to show—high-profile AI-sourced results have mostly produced unphysical materials or ones that were novel in trivial ways. And worse yet, the most promising evidence of AI speeding up materials science turned out to be completely fabricated.
paras.zh: 事实上，预测和设计新颖材料的能力历来被视为人工智能最伟大的承诺之一。然而，到目前为止，还没有什么可展示的——备受瞩目的人工智能结果大多产生了非物理材料或在琐碎方面新颖的材料。更糟糕的是，人工智能加速材料科学发展的最有希望的证据被证明是完全捏造的。

paras.en: Leslie Schoop, a physical chemist at Princeton University, who is also consulting with Anthropic, says these dubious past results may not forecast future performance. The dramatic jump in AI’s abilities over the past few months, she says, is undeniable. “It can now do mostly what I can do, except it doesn’t have a lab,” Schoop quips. Recently, she has been trying to coax AI models to predict the existence of a novel structure that she and her co-workers discovered in her lab through the old-fashioned combination of serendipity, intuition and repetition; none have succeeded. “The reason [AI] can’t find this structure is that there’s no analytical way to do it,” she says.
paras.zh: 普林斯顿大学物理化学家莱斯利·肖普 (Leslie Schoop) 也在为 Anthropic 提供咨询，他表示过去这些可疑的结果可能无法预测未来的表现。她说，过去几个月人工智能能力的急剧提升是不可否认的。 “它现在可以做我能做的大部分事情，只是它没有实验室，”斯科普打趣道。最近，她一直试图引导人工智能模型预测一种新颖结构的存在，这种结构是她和她的同事在实验室中通过偶然性、直觉和重复的老式组合发现的。但没有一个成功。 “[人工智能] 无法找到这种结构的原因是没有分析方法可以做到这一点，”她说。

paras.en: Of all the areas where AI is likely to struggle, perhaps the most ironic would be the study of intelligence itself and how it arises within the brain. Yet that is precisely where Histed thinks current and near-future models may flounder. “My sense is that the hard questions in the field are really not going to be solved by adding intelligence,” he says.
paras.zh: 在人工智能可能陷入困境的所有领域中，最具讽刺意味的是对智能本身及其在大脑中如何产生的研究。然而，这正是希斯特德认为当前和不久的将来模型可能陷入困境的地方。 “我的感觉是，该领域的难题实际上无法通过增加智能来解决，”他说。

paras.en: What neuroscience needs instead are more and better data, Histed says, reeling off several examples from his “most wanted” list: better recordings of neural activity, more thorough studies of biological networks, new measurements using frontier technologies such as optogenetics, and so on.
paras.zh: 希斯特德说，神经科学需要的是更多更好的数据，并列举了他“最想要的”清单中的几个例子：更好的神经活动记录、对生物网络更彻底的研究、使用光遗传学等前沿技术的新测量等等。

paras.en: Even if AI gets access to more and higher quality data, there is a looming obstacle for neuroscience and any other sufficiently complicated field. “At some point the amount of data you need to estimate your downstream nonlinear function is greater than can be acquired before the heat death of the universe,” Histed says. In other words, the problem is chaos. The behavior of a chaotic system such as Earth’s weather—and perhaps the brain itself—can only be calculated so far in advance before infinitesimal initial changes magnify to dramatically diverge from expectations.
paras.zh: 即使人工智能可以获得更多、更高质量的数据，神经科学和任何其他足够复杂的领域也面临着迫在眉睫的障碍。希斯特德说：“在某些时候，估算下游非线性函数所需的数据量会大于宇宙热寂之前所能获取的数据量。”换句话说，问题是混乱。像地球天气这样的混沌系统的行为——也许还有大脑本身——只能提前计算出无限小的初始变化，然后放大到与预期的巨大偏差。

paras.en: In December 2025 Schwartz began feeding graduate-student-level physics problems to Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.5 model (the company has since released better, more powerful Opus iterations). The model, Schwartz says, had plenty of limitations, but “it would come back in two minutes with an answer rather than two weeks.” He then documented his experience with an “AI grad student,” calling it “the most important paper I’ve ever written.”
paras.zh: 2025 年 12 月，Schwartz 开始将研究生级别的物理问题输入 Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 4.5 模型（该公司此后发布了更好、更强大的 Opus 迭代）。施瓦茨说，该模型有很多局限性，但“它会在两分钟内返回答案，而不是两周。”然后，他记录了他与一位“人工智能研究生”的经历，称其为“我写过的最重要的论文”。

paras.en: Since then Schwartz has continued working with the latest models. The trick, he says, is to find “AI-shaped” problems. Last month he and his collaborators released 36 preprints across 22 areas on problems such as outlining the geological history of Earth’s atmospheric oxygen, extending the branches of phylogenetic trees and determining the demographics of sunspots. The diverse problems shared features such as checkability and robust data—and many involved importing a mathematical tool across disciplinary boundaries.
paras.zh: 从那时起，施瓦茨继续研究最新的模型。他说，诀窍是找到“人工智能型”问题。上个月，他和他的合作者发布了 22 个领域的 36 份预印本，涉及诸如概述地球大气氧的地质历史、扩展系统发育树的分支以及确定太阳黑子的人口统计等问题。不同的问题具有可检查性和可靠数据等共同特征，而且许多问题都涉及跨学科边界导入数学工具。

paras.en: To generate the results, Schwartz solicited help from experts in various fields. The context they provided was vital. In one case the model proudly announced it had found a way to make earthquake forecasting 15 percent better than current methods—a claim that Schwartz’s independent human expert easily refuted. “Claude convinced me that this was interesting, but then the expert said, ‘Not really,’” Schwartz says.
paras.zh: 为了得出结果，施瓦茨向各个领域的专家寻求帮助。他们提供的背景至关重要。在一个案例中，该模型自豪地宣布它找到了一种方法，可以使地震预报比现有方法提高 15%，这一说法很快就被施瓦茨的独立人类专家驳斥了。 “克劳德让我相信这很有趣，但随后专家说，‘不是真的，’”施瓦茨说。

paras.en: Over time, the differences between AI-shaped problems are likely to shrink, Schwartz says. Where will AI be in one year? By some estimates, we will be most of the way to an apocalypse. Schwartz is somewhat less pessimistic but says change will keep accelerating. For theoretical physics, he predicts, “the content of any paper we could write today, Claude could just generate by thinking.”
paras.zh: 施瓦茨说，随着时间的推移，人工智能问题之间的差异可能会缩小。一年后人工智能会在哪里？根据一些估计，我们将大部分走向世界末日。施瓦茨的悲观情绪有所减轻，但他表示变化将继续加速。他预测，对于理论物理学，“我们今天可以写的任何论文的内容，克劳德都可以通过思考来生成。”

paras.en: Schoop, on the other hand, is not convinced that AI capabilities will continue to progress at their current rate. “You know, every exponential rise eventually flattens out,” she says.
paras.zh: 另一方面，Schoop 并不相信人工智能能力会继续以目前的速度发展。 “你知道，每一次指数增长最终都会趋于平缓，”她说。

paras.en: Two years ago I wrote a “don’t panic” piece in which I argued that AI would become just another tool for human scientists. Proclamations of imminent, immense change seemed silly; back then models routinely failed to count the number of r’s in “strawberry.” The past nine months of developments have been humbling to watch. In math, AI is not just operating as a tool; humans are so far out of the loop in some cases that they simply do not understand the answers models have conjured from the agentic ether. But that is not yet the case in science. Compared with questions of pure logic, the measurements scientists make of our messy universe may better insulate them against the depredations of AI. To what extent, though?
paras.zh: 两年前，我写了一篇“不要惊慌”的文章，其中我认为人工智能将成为人类科学家的另一种工具。宣布即将发生的巨大变革似乎很愚蠢。当时的模型通常无法计算“草莓”中 r 的数量。过去九个月的事态发展令人震惊。在数学中，人工智能不仅仅是作为一种工具；更是一种工具。在某些情况下，人类根本不了解模型从代理以太中召唤出的答案。但科学上的情况还不是这样。与纯逻辑问题相比，科学家对我们混乱的宇宙所做的测量可能会更好地使他们免受人工智能的掠夺。但到什么程度呢？

paras.en: As a routine skeptic and someone who still does not use generative AI, I take no pleasure in reporting this: we are facing a fundamental shift in the way information is produced—an event in human history that will probably be as impactful as the invention of the printing press. AI is poised to disrupt the jobs of all knowledge workers, which includes scientists—and science journalists. What precisely this means for science, let alone society, remains unclear, but we’re all about to find out.
paras.zh: 作为一个惯常的怀疑论者和仍然不使用生成式人工智能的人，我并不乐意报道这一点：我们正面临着信息产生方式的根本转变——人类历史上的这一事件可能会像印刷机的发明一样具有影响力。人工智能将颠覆所有知识工作者的工作，其中包括科学家和科学记者。这对科学（更不用说社会）究竟意味着什么尚不清楚，但我们都将找到答案。

paras.en: “My wife hates AI. And a lot of people do. It’s scary, and it’s impersonal and inhuman, and it’s encroaching on who we are,” Schwartz says. “But as a scientist, I just can’t not use the best available tools to solve problems.”
paras.zh: “我的妻子讨厌人工智能。很多人都讨厌人工智能。它很可怕，而且没有人情味和不人性，而且它正在侵犯我们的身份，”施瓦茨说。 “但作为一名科学家，我不能不使用最好的可用工具来解决问题。”

articles.title: Can a microdose of Ozempic help you live longer?

paras.en: GLP-1 drugs are transforming medicine—from treating obesity to diabetes to kidney and heart disease to sleep apnea. And now some telehealth companies are pitching them as a potential route to something more elusive—a longer and healthier life.
paras.zh: GLP-1 药物正在改变医学——从治疗肥胖症到糖尿病，再到肾病和心脏病，再到睡眠呼吸暂停。现在，一些远程医疗公司将其视为实现更难以捉摸的目标（更长寿、更健康的生活）的潜在途径。

paras.en: Specifically, microdoses of GLP-1s—little fractions of approved dose amounts—are being marketed as a way to tamp down inflammation, protect the brain and slow aging. A microdose of GLP-1 just means anything below the minimum dose approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Longevity influencer Bryan Johnson, for example, in 2024 described taking 0.5 milligrams of tirzepatide a week for longevity. He quit a few weeks later after his resting heart rate increased, however. And all promise of microdosing stems from a still-emerging body of evidence—a lot of which is in animals.
paras.zh: 具体来说，微剂量的 GLP-1（批准剂量的一小部分）正在作为一种抑制炎症、保护大脑和延缓衰老的方法进行销售。微剂量的 GLP-1 仅指低于美国食品和药物管理局批准的最小剂量的任何剂量。例如，长寿影响者 Bryan Johnson 在 2024 年描述了每周服用 0.5 毫克替泽帕肽可以延长寿命。然而，几周后，由于静息心率升高，他退出了。所有微剂量的希望都源于不断出现的证据——其中很多是在动物身上。

paras.en: There are decades of research showing that calorie restriction extends lifespan. Because GLP-1 drugs reduce food consumption, researchers wondered whether they could mimic this effect. “It was kind of logical to think about drugs that reduce calorie intake and reduce weight,” says Nicolas Musi, an endocrinologist who directs the Diabetes and Aging Center at Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles. But for years it remained a theory, he says.
paras.zh: 数十年的研究表明，热量限制可以延长寿命。由于 GLP-1 药物可以减少食物消耗，研究人员想知道它们是否可以模仿这种效果。 “考虑使用减少卡路里摄入量和减轻体重的药物是合乎逻辑的，”洛杉矶锡达斯西奈糖尿病和衰老中心主任内分泌学家尼古拉斯·穆西 (Nicolas Musi) 说。但他说，多年来这仍然是一个理论。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In September Danica Chen, a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, and her team found evidence that GLP-1s might have an effect on longevity in mice. Twenty-month-old female mice that were given daily semaglutide injections ate about a quarter less than control mice and lived almost 100 days longer. They also scored better on strength and memory testing and showed fewer molecular signs of aging, such as inflammation.
paras.zh: 9 月，加州大学伯克利分校教授 Danica Chen 和她的团队发现了 GLP-1 可能对小鼠寿命有影响的证据。每天注射索马鲁肽的 20 个月大雌性小鼠的食量比对照组小鼠少约四分之一，寿命延长了近 100 天。他们在力量和记忆测试中得分也更高，并且显示出更少的衰老分子迹象，例如炎症。

paras.en: To see whether eating less explained these effects, the researchers compared the drug with a diet that reduced food by the same amount. The two treatments had similar effects in several areas, but on measures of memory, exploratory behavior and blood sugar control, the semaglutide mice outperformed the calorie-restricted mice, suggesting “some mechanism that is independent of reduced food intake,” Chen says. The study used a dose equivalent to the standard. “We don’t know whether microdosing would have the same benefits,” she says.
paras.zh: 为了了解少吃是否可以解释这些影响，研究人员将该药物与减少相同量食物的饮食进行了比较。两种治疗方法在多个领域具有相似的效果，但在记忆、探索行为和血糖控制方面，索马鲁肽小鼠的表现优于热量限制小鼠，这表明“存在某种与食物摄入量减少无关的机制”，Chen 说。该研究使用了与标准相当的剂量。 “我们不知道微剂量是否会有同样的好处，”她说。

paras.en: The mouse data on longevity “is very, very compelling,” Chen says. “But before we get the data in humans, we just cannot say for sure.”
paras.zh: 陈说，关于寿命的小鼠数据“非常非常引人注目”。 “但在我们获得人体数据之前，我们还不能确定。”

paras.en: Post hoc analyses of human trials suggest GLP-1s slow molecular clocks that estimate biological age, which hints that the drugs might do more than just promote weight loss. But these trials have relied on standard doses rather than microdoses and are often in people who are overweight or have other comorbidities. Whether GLP-1s might extend the lives of healthy people, at any dose, remains unclear.
paras.zh: 对人体试验的事后分析表明，GLP-1 会减慢估计生物年龄的分子时钟，这暗示这些药物的作用可能不仅仅是促进减肥。但这些试验依赖于标准剂量而不是微剂量，并且通常是在超重或患有其他合并症的人群中进行。无论剂量如何，GLP-1 是否可以延长健康人的生命仍不清楚。

paras.en: In a small trial of adults with HIV and excess abdominal fat, semaglutide slowed their epigenetic clocks, which estimates biological age. When the team accounted for changes in body mass index and inflammation, some of the benefits remained. “It’s not completely just due to weight loss,” says Michael Corley, an aging researcher at the University of California, San Diego, who led the study.
paras.zh: 在一项针对患有艾滋病毒和腹部脂肪过多的成年人的小型试验中，索马鲁肽减慢了他们的表观遗传时钟，该时钟可估计生物年龄。当研究小组考虑到体重指数和炎症的变化时，一些好处仍然存在。 “这并不完全是因为体重减轻，”领导这项研究的加州大学圣地亚哥分校老龄化研究员迈克尔·科利 (Michael Corley) 说。

paras.en: Other studies have found similar results. In October Novo Nordisk, which makes Wegovy and Ozempic, presented new analyses of their earlier trials at a longevity research conference. In a preprint that hasn’t been peer-reviewed, the hearts, kidneys and brains of people on semaglutide appeared up to four years younger based on organ-specific biological aging clocks.
paras.zh: 其他研究也发现了类似的结果。 10 月，Wegovy 和 Ozempic 的生产商诺和诺德在一次长寿研究会议上展示了对其早期试验的新分析。在一份未经同行评审的预印本中，根据器官特异性生物衰老时钟，服用索马鲁肽的人的心脏、肾脏和大脑似乎年轻了四岁。

paras.en: Musi says it’s too early to say if the drugs extend life or improve health over the long term, and exactly how GLP-1s might exert these effects is also unclear. Eating less and losing weight can reduce inflammation on their own, so some benefits may be indirect, Musi says. But there are some “hints” of direct effects of the drugs, he says.
paras.zh: Musi 表示，从长远来看，判断这些药物是否能延长生命或改善健康还为时过早，而且 GLP-1 究竟如何发挥这些作用也尚不清楚。穆西说，少吃和减肥本身就可以减轻炎症，因此一些好处可能是间接的。但他说，有一些药物的直接影响的“迹象”。

paras.en: It’s possible that the drugs could be influencing several processes thought to drive aging. One of these is chronic inflammation, which rises with age and is linked to heart disease and dementia. Another is cellular senescence, in which damaged cells stop dividing by remaining in tissues, and the decline of mitochondria, which supply cells with energy. In Chen’s mouse study, semaglutide reduced inflammation, cellular senescence and mitochondrial damage. But whether microdoses might show these same signals remains to be seen.
paras.zh: 这些药物可能会影响多个被认为会导致衰老的过程。其中之一是慢性炎症，它随着年龄的增长而增加，并与心脏病和痴呆症有关。另一个是细胞衰老，受损细胞因保留在组织中而停止分裂，以及为细胞提供能量的线粒体的衰退。在 Chen 的小鼠研究中，索马鲁肽可以减少炎症、细胞衰老和线粒体损伤。但微剂量是否会显示出这些相同的信号还有待观察。

paras.en: Most of the evidence for taking a smaller dose is for those trying to keep weight off. But microdoses are far smaller and may not deliver the benefits seen at full doses, Musi says. Many products sold as microdoses are also compounded, so they aren’t regulated by the FDA in the same way as approved drugs. As a result, some people may be taking different formulations than they think, Corley says.
paras.zh: 大多数服用较小剂量的证据是针对那些试图减肥的人。但穆西说，微剂量要小得多，可能无法带来全剂量的好处。许多以微剂量销售的产品也是复合的，因此它们不受 FDA 与批准药物相同的监管。因此，有些人采取的配方可能与他们想象的不同，科利说。

paras.en: For any healthy person considering microdosing GLP-1s for longevity, “I would definitely not recommend it at this point,” Corley says. Diet, exercise and sleep are still the gold standard, he says, and for someone already working on those, “there’s no indication that adding GLP-1s with microdosing is going to make a meaningful benefit.”
paras.zh: 对于任何考虑服用微量 GLP-1 来延长寿命的健康人来说，“我目前绝对不会推荐它，”Corley 说。他说，饮食、锻炼和睡眠仍然是黄金标准，对于已经在这些方面开展工作的人来说，“没有迹象表明添加微剂量的 GLP-1 会产生有意义的益处。”

articles.title: Science to restore speech is moving fast. Here’s what’s next
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Scientists are racing to restore people’s ability to communicate. Powerful AI-based methods to decode speech signals and predict words, along with advances in technology, promise success.
paras.zh: 科学家们正在竞相恢复人们的沟通能力。强大的基于人工智能的方法来解码语音信号和预测单词，加上技术的进步，有望取得成功。

paras.en: This episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me takes listeners through the breadth of scientific efforts to restore words, emotions and even gestures to people who can’t move or talk.
paras.zh: 这一集《深渊：对我说话》将带领听众了解科学努力的广度，以帮助无法移动或说话的人恢复言语、情感甚至手势。

paras.en: We’ll hear from Casey Harrell, a man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis who can no longer talk. A user of today’s technology, Harrell has a unique perspective on what he’d like to see improved for the technology of tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我们将听到凯西·哈雷尔 (Casey Harrell) 的来信，他患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症，无法说话。作为当今技术的用户，哈勒尔对于他希望看到未来技术的改进有着独特的视角。

paras.en: And as season two wraps up, listeners will be left with a reminder of the power of a voice: a piece of comedy from Jules Rodriguez, performed with his voice clone in front of a live crowd.
paras.zh: 随着第二季的结束，听众将记住声音的力量：朱尔斯·罗德里格斯的一部喜剧，在现场观众面前用他的声音克隆表演。

paras.en: “Being backstage and then seeing him come out, like, roll out his wheelchair, and everybody goes nuts because they’re like, ‘What is going on here? This doesn’t make sense,’” says Jules’ wife, Maria Aleandra Fernandez. “And every time I was like, ‘This is life. This is love. This is passion. What else is there?’ I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here.”
paras.zh: “在后台，然后看到他出来，就像推出轮椅一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会说，‘这里发生了什么事？这没有道理，’”朱尔斯的妻子玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯 (Maria Aleandra Fernandez) 说道。 “每次我都会想，‘这就是生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。还有什么？’我不知道还有什么比这个家伙在这里所做的事情更强大的了。”

paras.en: Laura Sanders: OK, I want to ask who your favorite comedians are and why. Who makes you all laugh?
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：好的，我想问你最喜欢的喜剧演员是谁以及为什么。谁让大家笑了？

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: Pete Holmes and Mike Birbiglia are some of my favorites.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：皮特·霍尔姆斯和迈克·比尔比利亚是我的最爱。

paras.en: [Audio] He was just like, I’m a bear, et cetera.
paras.zh: [音频]他就像，我是一只熊，等等。

paras.en: [Audio] The best part of sleep is falling asleep. That’s the only part you’re there for.
paras.zh: [音频] 睡眠最好的部分就是入睡。这是你唯一要做的事情。

paras.en: Jules: Their styles are different, but I have always gravitated towards their authenticity.
paras.zh: Jules：他们的风格不同，但我一直偏向于他们的真实性。

paras.en: Sanders: There’s another comedian who is extra meaningful for Jules: Conan O’Brien.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：还有一位喜剧演员对朱尔斯来说特别有意义：柯南·奥布莱恩。

paras.en: [Audio] Today is a bit of a different sort of episode. I’ll be talking to Jules and Maria.
paras.zh: [音频] 今天的情节有点不同。我要和朱尔斯和玛丽亚说话。

paras.en: Sanders: After MA had reached out, Conan invited the couple onto his podcast, where they connected about comedy. Conan still checks in on Jules every so often.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：MA 联系后，柯南邀请这对夫妇加入他的播客，他们在那里谈论喜剧。柯南仍然时不时地来看望朱尔斯。

paras.en: [Audio] It’s incredible to me that in our conversations, you’re very frank about the pain that you go through, and how intense it is. But you’re also always so positive and funny and, frankly, you give me a lot of [beep]. Which I find to be, well I hate it, by the way, first of all. Oh, get over it, Conan.
paras.zh: [音频]令我难以置信的是，在我们的谈话中，你非常坦率地讲述了你所经历的痛苦，以及它有多么强烈。但你也总是那么积极、有趣，坦率地说，你给了我很多[嘟嘟]。我发现，顺便说一句，首先，我讨厌它。哦，克服它，柯南。

paras.en: Jules: Conan is very special to me. Watching and listening to him helped me disconnect from the harsh reality of my life. And when I got to meet him and chat with him, it meant the world to me.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：柯南对我来说很特别。观看和聆听他的讲话帮助我摆脱了生活中严酷的现实。当我见到他并与他聊天时，这对我来说意味着整个世界。

paras.en: Maria Aleandra Fernandez: Having the most normal conversation with Conan O’Brien is something I will never get over.
paras.zh: 玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯：与柯南·奥布莱恩进行最正常的对话是我永远无法克服的事情。

paras.en: [Audio] So he has a bunch of banked phrases. He’s going to play a few of our favorites. OK. I’m fine. I’m perfectly [beep] fine. [laughter] Come on man, are we doing this or not? Oh my God, oh my God. I’m destroying this marriage.
paras.zh: [音频]所以他有一堆储存的短语。他将演奏一些我们最喜欢的曲目。好的。我很好。我很好[哔]很好。 [笑声]来吧伙计，我们到底要不要这样做？天啊，天啊。我正在毁掉这段婚姻。

paras.en: MA: He really is so genuine and like, not only willing to talk to us, but really looks forward to talking. Like, I love talking to you guys. I’m not just doing it to be a nice person, which feels, you know, feels wonderful.
paras.zh: MA：他真的很真诚，很喜欢，不仅愿意和我们交谈，而且真的很期待交谈。就像，我喜欢和你们聊天。我这样做不仅仅是为了成为一个好人，这感觉，你知道，感觉很棒。

paras.en: [Audio] You have my love, my respect and we’re thinking about you guys all the time.
paras.zh: [音频]你们拥有我的爱、我的尊重，我们一直在想着你们。

paras.en: Sanders: As you were talking earlier, it made me think about what it means to make somebody laugh and to entertain them, and like how actually very, very special that must be. Just kind of, at its heart, it’s, it is joy and humans connecting. And so, extra special.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：正如你之前所说，这让我思考让别人发笑并娱乐他们意味着什么，并且喜欢这实际上是非常非常特别的。从本质上讲，它是快乐和人类的联系。所以，格外特别。

paras.en: MA: That’s the other thing I’ve learned mainly through Jules, about humor and comedy. And who were we watching yesterday? The NPR interview with Dave Chappelle.
paras.zh: MA：这是我主要通过朱尔斯学到的另一件事，关于幽默和喜剧。昨天我们看谁了？美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 采访戴夫·查佩尔 (Dave Chappelle)。

paras.en: [Audio] Dave Chappelle says he is very clear about his role as a comedian.
paras.zh: [音频]戴夫·查普尔说他非常清楚自己作为喜剧演员的角色。

paras.en: MA: And Dave Chappelle said something that is so spot-on. He said that comedians are how people metabolize things.
paras.zh: MA：戴夫·查佩尔（Dave Chappelle）说了一些非常准确的话。他说喜剧演员就是人们代谢事物的方式。

paras.en: [Audio] We’re like the nation’s kidney. We help everyone metabolize not just facts, but feelings around facts, or ideas. And jokes are just a shorthand for all of that.
paras.zh: [音频]我们就像国家的肾脏。我们不仅帮助每个人代谢事实，还帮助每个人代谢事实或想法的感受。笑话只是所有这一切的简写。

paras.en: MA: And I’m also a nerd and I’ve been reading some Greek tragedies and studying about how, you know, that’s also like the artists that help people metabolize feelings and emotions. And when he said that, I was like, that’s exactly it. And that’s what Jules has done.
paras.zh: MA：我也是一个书呆子，我一直在读一些希腊悲剧，并研究如何，你知道，这也像艺术家一样帮助人们代谢感觉和情绪。当他这么说时，我想，就是这样。这就是朱尔斯所做的。

paras.en: It’s something that heals. And it’s not even like it’s self-deprecating. It’s not like, oh, let’s make fun. And the way he does it is so smart and genuine, but also not taking himself seriously. It just disarms everything. You’re just like, oh, OK. And that idea of metabolizing the really hard feelings that come around grief, mortality, losing a person, seeing how he’s trapped in his body, but he chooses not to be trapped in that really big way is so profound.
paras.zh: 这是一种可以治愈的东西。而且这甚至不像是自嘲。这不像是，哦，让我们开玩笑吧。他的做法是如此聪明和真诚，但也不把自己当回事。它只会解除一切武装。你就像，哦，好吧。代谢掉悲伤、死亡、失去一个人所带来的真正痛苦的感觉，看到他如何被困在自己的身体里，但他选择不被困在那个真正的大方式中，这种想法是如此深刻。

paras.en: Sanders: Science is iterative. It builds. It may take a wrong turn or two, but overall, it’s moving toward a deeper understanding of our world and of ourselves.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：科学是迭代的。它建立了。它可能会走一两个错误的弯路，但总的来说，它正在朝着对我们的世界和我们自己有更深入的了解的方向发展。

paras.en: By using their voices, by telling their stories, by telling their jokes, Jules and MA are helping me, and maybe you too, metabolize the pain – and the joy – of living. Welcome to The Deep End, Talk to Me.
paras.zh: 通过使用他们的声音，通过讲述他们的故事，通过讲他们的笑话，朱尔斯和马正在帮助我，也许你也是，代谢生活中的痛苦和快乐。欢迎来到深渊，跟我说话。

paras.en: [Voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? Hi. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？你好。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。

paras.en: Sanders: I’m Laura Sanders and today, we’re going to look ahead to what’s coming next for the human voice and efforts to restore it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我是劳拉·桑德斯，今天，我们将展望人类声音的下一步发展以及恢复它的努力。

paras.en: Sanders: In some ways, this podcast is a story of progress, of figuring out, little by little, more about the brain, and more about technology and more about people. Today, Jules can type with his eyes, and his son can hear his dad’s voice say I love you. In earlier episodes, you heard from Casey Harrell. Casey can think about saying a word to his daughter, and boom, they’re off playing a game together.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从某些方面来说，这个播客是一个关于进步的故事，一个关于一点一点地弄清楚更多关于大脑、更多关于技术和更多关于人的故事。今天，朱尔斯可以用眼睛打字，他的儿子可以听到父亲的声音说我爱你。在之前的剧集中，您听到了凯西·哈勒尔的来信。凯西可以考虑对他的女儿说一句话，然后，他们就一起去玩游戏了。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: So this has kept me still in touch with people and the world, and it is not hyperbole to frame it this way.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔：所以这让我仍然与人们和世界保持联系，这样说并不夸张。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey has ALS and can no longer speak. He volunteered for a clinical trial, and now he has a device implanted in his brain that detects neural patterns as he tries to say a word. This system has changed his life.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症，无法说话。他自愿参加一项临床试验，现在他的大脑中植入了一个装置，可以在他试图说话时检测神经模式。这个系统改变了他的生活。

paras.en: Casey: It is the ability to parent my daughter. It is the ability to connect with my wife. It is the ability to make a wry joke with my friends. Timing is everything, and that is why having nothing, this is completely revolutionary.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是养育女儿的能力。这是与我妻子联系的能力。这是与朋友开玩笑的能力。时机就是一切，这就是为什么什么都没有，这是完全革命性的。

paras.en: Sanders: But there aren’t many people like Casey. Leigh Hochberg is the director of the BrainGate clinical trials consortium, the trial that Casey is participating in. I asked him how many people might have participated in similar sorts of research projects. How many people have electrodes in their brain that can help them speak?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是像凯西这样的人并不多。 Leigh Hochberg 是 BrainGate 临床试验联盟的主任，Casey 正在参与该试验。我问他可能有多少人参与过类似的研究项目。有多少人的大脑中有可以帮助他们说话的电极？

paras.en: Leigh Hochberg: In terms of actually decoding attempted speech, I’m almost sure it’s still less than 10. It may be closer to five or six, so far, and that number undoubtedly is going to increase fairly quickly.
paras.zh: Leigh Hochberg：就实际解码尝试的语音而言，我几乎可以肯定它仍然少于 10 个。到目前为止，它可能接近 5 个或 6 个，而且这个数字无疑会很快增加。

paras.en: Sanders: So this is a small but growing number. Growing, because we now have a solid scientific understanding of the brain’s speech signals, and other signals too. And neurotech companies are very interested.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以这是一个很小但不断增长的数字。不断增长，因为我们现在对大脑的语音信号和其他信号有了扎实的科学理解。神经科技公司对此非常感兴趣。

paras.en: Hochberg: About 10 years ago or so, the academic research had de-risked this field sufficiently that it allowed for the entry of now likely a dozen or more companies that are actively pursuing their own version of an implantable brain-computer interface.
paras.zh: Hochberg：大约十年前，学术研究已经充分降低了这一领域的风险，以至于现在可能有十几家或更多的公司进入该领域，这些公司正在积极开发自己的可植入脑机接口版本。

paras.en: What I anticipate will happen, what I guess I hope will happen, is that the companies will continue to very carefully, thoughtfully and in a very focused manner, create their systems, and test them rigorously. And hopefully they’ll be demonstrated to be safe and effective. And at the same time, the academic groups have the opportunity to continue to demonstrate what’s possible, to push beyond that, and to show hopefully what those medical devices, once they’re actually available to market, might be able to do next.
paras.zh: 我预计将会发生的事情，我想我希望将会发生的事情是，这些公司将继续非常仔细、深思熟虑、以非常专注的方式创建他们的系统，并严格测试它们。希望它们能被证明是安全有效的。与此同时，学术团体有机会继续展示可能性，超越这一点，并希望展示这些医疗设备一旦真正推向市场，下一步可能能够做什么。

paras.en: Sanders: I talked with Vikash Gilja, a neural engineer who works at a company called Paradromics. He sees this momentum that Hochberg describes too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我与 Vikash Gilja 进行了交谈，他是一名神经工程师，在一家名为 Paradromics 的公司工作。他也看到了霍赫伯格所描述的这种势头。

paras.en: Vikash Gilja: And, you know, we can see all the pieces coming together. These tools weren’t available even five years ago. And what we’re seeing is like, you know, month over month, there are new tools available. So we’re able to leverage those and move faster.
paras.zh: Vikash Gilja：而且，你知道，我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。这些工具在五年前还没有出现。我们看到的是，你知道，每个月都有新的工具可用。因此，我们能够利用这些并更快地采取行动。

paras.en: Sanders: Paradromics has developed its own brain-computer interface for communication. The device is about the size of a dime, and it sits on the motor cortex. That’s the part of the brain that creates speech signals. The chip then detects these signals as a person thinks about saying a word.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：Paradromics 开发了自己的用于通信的脑机接口。该设备大约有一毛钱大小，位于运动皮层上。这是大脑中产生语音信号的部分。当一个人想要说一个词时，芯片就会检测到这些信号。

paras.en: Matthew Willsey: So the cortical module has 421 tiny little sensors.
paras.zh: Matthew Willsey：皮质模块有 421 个微小的传感器。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s neurosurgeon and biomedical engineer Matthew Willsey, of the University of Michigan Health. He’s describing the device from Paradromics here.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是密歇根大学健康分校的神经外科医生和生物医学工程师马修·威尔西。他在这里描述了 Paradromics 的设备。

paras.en: Willsey: They’re about one and a half millimeters long. And you know, it’s smaller than your thumbnail, like kind of all the way around. It’s like a cylinder. And at the bottom of the cylinder are the electrodes, is what we call them. And we get them really close to the brain. And then when we deploy it, what it does is it pushes those electrodes down into the brain.
paras.zh: 威尔西：它们大约一毫米半长。你知道，它比你的缩略图还要小，就像周围一样。它就像一个圆柱体。圆柱体的底部是电极，就是我们所说的电极。我们让它们非常接近大脑。然后当我们部署它时，它的作用是将这些电极向下推入大脑。

paras.en: Sanders: Those tiny sensors are listening to the nearby neurons that control the muscles required for speech.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些微小的传感器正在聆听附近控制言语所需肌肉的神经元的声音。

paras.en: Willsey: The principle is to try and get these things as small as possible to disrupt the least amount of tissue as possible, and then to get them really, really close to the individual cells, the neurons themselves that have the information we’re trying to record.
paras.zh: Willsey：原则是尝试让这些东西尽可能小，以尽可能少地破坏组织，然后让它们真正非常接近单个细胞，即拥有我们试图记录信息的神经元本身。

paras.en: Sanders: The goal here is to restore a person’s ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这里的目标是恢复一个人的说话能力。

paras.en: Willsey: So in the ideal situation, the electrodes would sit, you know, right next to those neurons. This type of technology that’s very intuitive, that can record activity from the brain in kind of a high-throughput way, can put the words up at a good speed and a good accuracy, allows them to kind of regain the ability to communicate with others close to how they maybe were before they had the illness. So that truly is very powerful.
paras.zh: 威尔西：所以在理想情况下，电极应该位于那些神经元旁边。这种非常直观的技术，可以以高通量的方式记录大脑的活动，可以以良好的速度和良好的准确性说出单词，使他们能够重新获得与他人沟通的能力，接近他们患病之前的状态。所以这确实是非常强大的。

paras.en: Sanders: You might remember that Casey’s implant, called the BrainGate 2 system, requires ports on his head that are connected to external wires.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：你可能还记得凯西的植入物，称为 BrainGate 2 系统，需要他头上的端口连接到外部电线。

paras.en: Casey: What is annoying about this device is really easy to answer. It is not portable, and it is not implanted only inside my head.
paras.zh: 凯西：这个设备令人烦恼的地方很容易回答。它不是便携式的，也不是只植入我的脑袋里。

paras.en: Sanders: Unlike Casey’s implant, the Paradromics device is fully implantable. That means it’s wireless. This summer, Willsey implanted Paradromic’s device in a volunteer’s brain. The brain belonged to a 68-year-old woman who lives in Michigan. She has primary lateral sclerosis, a disease that has taken away most of her ability to talk. So far, the Paradromics system is up and running, and the volunteer is testing her abilities out.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：与凯西的植入物不同，Paradromics 设备是完全可植入的。这意味着它是无线的。今年夏天，威尔西将 Paradromic 的设备植入一名志愿者的大脑中。大脑属于一位居住在密歇根州的 68 岁女性。她患有原发性侧索硬化症，这种疾病剥夺了她大部分说话的能力。到目前为止，Paradromics 系统已经启动并运行，志愿者正在测试她的能力。

paras.en: Here she is talking with Willsey and other researchers in a video provided by Paradromics. You’ll hear her natural voice, which is hard to understand, and then a digital voice speaking the words her brain implant decoded.
paras.zh: 在 Paradromics 提供的视频中，她正在与威尔西和其他研究人员交谈。你会听到她自然的声音，这很难理解，然后是一个数字声音，说出她的大脑植入解码的单词。

paras.en: [Audio] I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. Yeah, it’s good.
paras.zh: [音频]我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。是的，这很好。

paras.en: Sanders: This volunteer has used the device to talk to her grandkids on the phone. But this is just the very beginning for this research project. There’s so much more to test.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这位志愿者使用该设备与她的孙子们通电话。但这只是这个研究项目的开始。还有很多东西需要测试。

paras.en: Casey is still working on his system, too — particularly, streamlining the process. When Casey uses his brain-computer interface, it decodes speech signals from his brain, then puts words on a screen. Casey then selects a button, using his eye movements or his brain-computer interface, to say these words out loud with a digital voice. Here’s Casey.
paras.zh: 凯西仍在研究他的系统，特别是简化流程。当凯西使用他的脑机接口时，它会解码来自他大脑的语音信号，然后将文字显示在屏幕上。然后凯西使用他的眼球运动或脑机接口选择一个按钮，用数字声音大声说出这些词。这是凯西。

paras.en: Casey: It is not fast enough to provide enough instant conversation with other people that need to slow down to talk to me.
paras.zh: 凯西：它的速度不够快，无法与其他需要放慢速度与我交谈的人提供足够的即时对话。

paras.en: Sanders: But scientists want to skip this middle part — the words written on a screen. They want instead to go straight to speech, and perhaps make conversations faster. Casey says this goal to go directly from brain signals to a speaking digital voice would be his top priority.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是科学家们想跳过中间部分——屏幕上写的文字。相反，他们希望直接开始讲话，也许可以让对话更快。凯西表示，将大脑信号直接转化为数字语音的目标将是他的首要任务。

paras.en: Casey: That one is the holy grail of what this will become in terms of speech. It will allow you to have a seamless conversation. I am talking about, yes, I will intend to talk, and then it will just translate that automatically into speech, like we do, and you are doing right now.
paras.zh: 凯西：这就是演讲方面的圣杯。它将使您能够进行无缝的对话。我说的是，是的，我打算说话，然后它会自动将其转化为言语，就像我们所做的那样，而你现在正在做的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: In an earlier episode, we talked about attempts to do just this with Casey’s system, to push it to do what they call brain-to-voice. Early attempts were hard to decipher. But it has already improved, by a lot. In the latest tests, this brain-to-voice process produces words that are understandable – reaching about 95 percent accuracy for listeners. Here’s Casey speaking test sentences. It comes from a preprint manuscript posted on the website bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在之前的一集中，我们谈到了尝试用凯西的系统来做到这一点，推动它做他们所谓的大脑到声音的事情。早期的尝试很难破译。但它已经改善了很多。在最新的测试中，这种大脑到声音的过程产生了可以理解的单词——对于听众来说，准确率达到了 95% 左右。这是凯西口语测试句子。它来自 bioRxiv 网站上发布的预印本手稿。

paras.en: [Audio] The day is not over yet. Please come in with me.
paras.zh: [音频] 这一天还没有结束。请跟我进来。

paras.en: Sanders: Scientists have another thing on their to-do list. And this one goes beyond the words themselves. Here’s Gilja, from Paradromics.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：科学家们的待办事项清单上还有另一件事。这超出了言语本身。这是来自 Paradromics 的 Gilja。

paras.en: Gilja: Let’s say I identify whether a sentence is a statement or a question. Well, now you can pass that information on to speech synthesis, so that you get these two different versions.
paras.zh: Gilja：假设我识别一个句子是陈述还是问题。好吧，现在您可以将该信息传递给语音合成，以便获得这两个不同的版本。

paras.en: Sanders: The same words could be a statement or a question. You see what he means. You see what he means? And that information can be pulled out from a person’s brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：同样的词可以是陈述，也可以是问题。你明白他的意思。你明白他的意思吗？这些信息可以从一个人的大脑活动中提取出来。

paras.en: Gilja: If I’m decoding prosodic information, if I’m decoding speed, when a word is meant to appear, that can also be passed on to modern speech synthesis systems, so that you’re more accurately capturing the prosody that somebody intends. Same thing with loudness, right? So you can see how as that information becomes available from the neural channels, it can be provided to the AI speech synthesis to get closer to the intended voice in the moment that the individual wants to generate.
paras.zh: Gilja：如果我正在解码韵律信息，如果我正在解码速度，当一个单词应该出现时，它也可以传递到现代语音合成系统，这样你就可以更准确地捕捉某人想要的韵律。响度也是一样，对吧？因此，您可以看到，当神经通道提供这些信息时，如何将其提供给人工智能语音合成，以更接近个人想要生成的时刻的预期声音。

paras.en: Sanders: All of these signals can be collected and used to build a more accurate voice — one that says things exactly how a person intends to say them, like a Minnesotan’s ooftah or a slow southern hey y’all. Now, today’s voice clones can add these emotional layers onto words already. Here’s what Jules told me when I asked him about whether his voice clone can do it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所有这些信号都可以被收集并用来构建更准确的声音——一种完全按照一个人想要说的方式说话的声音，就像明尼苏达州的“ooftah”或缓慢的南方“嘿，大家”。现在，今天的语音克隆已经可以将这些情感层添加到单词中。当我问朱尔斯他的声音克隆能否做到这一点时，这是朱尔斯告诉我的。

paras.en: Jules: Oh, there are plenty of things it does that are all the above. But one thing in particular is how it inserts tone and inflections on words. Sometimes my wife will get mad because my response can come off with some sass.
paras.zh: Jules：哦，它做了很多事情，就是上面提到的。但特别的一件事是它如何在单词中插入语气和变化。有时我的妻子会生气，因为我的回答可能有些无礼。

paras.en: Sanders: So there’s loudness, emphasis, pitch — all of these things contribute to what words means. But imagine if a brain implant can pick up these cues directly — no typing required. Here’s Hochberg.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以有响度、强调、音调——所有这些因素都有助于表达单词的含义。但想象一下，如果大脑植入物可以直接接收这些线索——无需打字。这是霍赫伯格。

paras.en: Hochberg: There’s a lot that can be conveyed through the emphasis, through the tone, through even the humor that can sometimes be conveyed by the way that somebody who’s able-bodied may speak a particular sentence. All of those, I think, really can be captured by these implantable brain-computer interfaces by harnessing the rich neural activity that’s available from the brain. We should be able to restore a lot of that.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：通过强调、语气、甚至幽默，可以传达很多东西，有时可以通过身体健全的人说某个特定句子的方式来传达。我认为，所有这些都可以通过利用大脑丰富的神经活动，通过这些植入式脑机接口来捕获。我们应该能够恢复很多。

paras.en: Sanders: Sergey Stavisky is one of the UC Davis researchers working with Casey and Hochberg. He and his colleagues are working on some of these ideas.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西和霍赫伯格一起工作。他和他的同事正在研究其中一些想法。

paras.en: Stavisky: And even now we’re continuing to improve that and actually adding additional layers. So we have one forward-looking project where we can maybe decode the kind of emotional valence of how he’s trying to say it. Is he trying to say something in an angry way or in a surprised way or in a happy-sounding way, to kind of further make it more expressive.
paras.zh: Stavisky：即使是现在，我们仍在继续改进这一点，并实际上添加了额外的层。因此，我们有一个前瞻性的项目，我们也许可以解读他试图表达的情感价值。他是否试图以愤怒的方式、惊讶的方式或听起来快乐的方式说某事，以进一步使其更具表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: They’re even trying to decode singing. Well, OK, it’s really more of a hum at this point, he says. But those sorts of tone shifts could, in theory, be deciphered.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们甚至试图解码歌唱。好吧，好吧，现在更多的是嗡嗡声，他说。但从理论上讲，这些语气转变是可以被解读的。

paras.en: Stavisky: We definitely have our work cut out for us on the singing and melody side of things.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：在歌唱和旋律方面，我们确实有很多工作要做。

paras.en: Sanders: All sorts of voice signals could be pulled from brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：各种声音信号都可以从大脑活动中提取。

paras.en: Stavisky: Ultimately, we want people to be in full control of what they’re communicating. This should come from their intent. So, yeah, we are trying to decode all of the aspects of his voice, whether it’s the pitch, the timbre, the loudness, the intonation, which word he’s stressing. All of that, ideally, we would decode from brain activity, including kind of all of that emotional nuance.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：最终，我们希望人们能够完全控制他们所交流的内容。这应该是出于他们的意图。所以，是的，我们正在尝试解码他声音的所有方面，无论是音调、音色、响度、语调，还是他强调的单词。理想情况下，我们可以从大脑活动中解码所有这些，包括所有情感上的细微差别。

paras.en: Sanders: Voice clones can speak with various emotions. You heard my voice clone do just that in earlier episodes. But the difference here is that a person wouldn’t have to type in the instructions. They would come straight from their brain, seamlessly. Other nonverbal signals can be pulled from the brain, too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音克隆可以表达各种情绪。你在之前的剧集中听到我的声音克隆就是这样做的。但这里的区别在于，人们不必输入说明。它们会直接来自他们的大脑，无缝地。其他非语言信号也可以从大脑中提取。

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: In the past five years or so, there have been a lot of advancements in the field of BCIs for restoring individual functions to people with paralysis.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：在过去五年左右的时间里，脑机接口领域在帮助瘫痪患者恢复个人功能方面取得了很多进展。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Samantha Brosler, a bioengineer at the University of California, San Francisco. Some brain-computer interfaces can pick up movements. We haven’t talked much about them, but these implants have their own very successful research history. They’ve allowed people to control a robotic arm, for instance.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是萨曼莎·布罗斯勒，加州大学旧金山分校的生物工程师。一些脑机接口可以接收动作。我们没有过多谈论它们，但这些植入物有自己非常成功的研究历史。例如，他们允许人们控制机械臂。

paras.en: Brosler: Most of these devices so far have been designed to restore one function at a time, whereas in reality, frequently people who are paralyzed are missing both the ability to speak and perform body movements. And so in this study, we asked whether a single brain implant could be used to decode both speech and movement at the same time.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：到目前为止，大多数这些设备的设计目的都是一次恢复一种功能，而实际上，瘫痪的人经常丧失说话和进行身体运动的能力。因此，在这项研究中，我们询问是否可以使用单个大脑植入物同时解码语音和运动。

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out, it could. She and her colleagues were able to decode gestures for communication — things like thumbs up, or a head nodding yes — and words. This combo approach is a more natural way of getting a point across.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明，可以。她和她的同事能够解读交流手势（例如竖起大拇指或点头表示同意）和言语。这种组合方法是一种更自然的表达观点的方式。

paras.en: Brosler: We naturally use gestures alongside our speech. So for example, some gestures can substitute for speech entirely, like nodding yes, shaking your head no, waving, shrugging, giving a thumbs up. But they can also add or change the meaning of what we’re saying. So for example, if you say maybe combined with nod head yes, that has a very different, you know, meaning than if you say maybe and shrug or shake your head no.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们在讲话时自然会使用手势。例如，某些手势可以完全替代言语，例如点头“是”、摇头“不”、挥手、耸肩、竖起大拇指。但他们也可以添加或改变我们所说的话的含义。例如，如果你说“也许”加上点头“是”，这与你说“也许”然后耸耸肩或摇头“不”的含义非常不同。

paras.en: Sanders: My kids know that a slow maybe with a skeptical eyebrow raise is much closer to a no than my fast upbeat maybe with a little head nod. There is so much subtext in our body language.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我的孩子们知道，缓慢地扬起怀疑的眉毛可能比我快速乐观地点头可能更接近于“不”。我们的肢体语言中有很多潜台词。

paras.en: Brosler: So I think of, you know, gestures and body movements as an additional communication channel that can work together with speech to add expressivity to what we’re trying to say.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：所以我认为，手势和身体动作是一种额外的沟通渠道，可以与语音一起工作，为我们想说的话增添表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: In the study, the output was a digital avatar who looked like the person. Success looked like the avatar moving and getting the word right.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在这项研究中，输出的是一个看起来像这个人的数字化身。成功看起来就像化身移动并正确表达了意思。

paras.en: Brosler: And the idea is that we enable the participants to use speech and gestures alone or together. So in theory, someone could say hello while waving.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们的想法是让参与者能够单独或一起使用语音和手势。所以理论上，有人可以一边挥手一边打招呼。

paras.en: Sanders: The researchers started simple, with just a few phrases — hello, bye, good idea, how’s it going, let’s go — and just a few gestures, like a shrug or a point, a fist pump, thumbs up.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：研究人员从简单的开始，只有几句话——你好、再见、好主意、怎么样、走吧——还有几个手势，比如耸肩或点一下、握拳、竖起大拇指。

paras.en: Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: Sanders: The sheer number of different approaches to restoring communication is a sign that this neurotechnology is coming fast. Here’s Willsey.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：恢复沟通的不同方法的数量之多表明这种神经技术正在快速发展。这是威尔西。

paras.en: Willsey: I think it’s good. There’s a lot of players that are entering into the field that have a variety of different ideas where they can run the clinical trials and see how these different devices stack up.
paras.zh: 威尔西：我认为这很好。许多进入该领域的参与者都有各种不同的想法，他们可以进行临床试验，看看这些不同的设备如何叠加。

paras.en: Sanders: There are lots of reasons to be optimistic about the future here, and it’s a future that isn’t even that far off. Here’s David Brandman, one of the researchers at UC Davis who works with Casey. He’s also the neurosurgeon who implanted Casey’s device.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有很多理由对这里的未来感到乐观，而且这个未来并不遥远。这是大卫·布兰德曼（David Brandman），他是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西一起工作。他也是植入凯西设备的神经外科医生。

paras.en: Brandman: I think I’m about five years away from being able to meet a patient with ALS and having the following conversation, and saying, you know, Ms. Smith, I’m sorry you’ve been diagnosed with ALS. I don’t have a cure for you, but I do have a device that I can implant that can help you communicate despite facing a future of paralysis. It’s a device that would be implanted. It’s fully wirelessly. It’s cosmetically invisible, and you’d be able to use it to communicate your needs and have a meaningful conversation with friends and family. So I think that kind of conversation is about five to 10 years away.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我想大约还有五年的时间我就能见到 ALS 患者并进行以下对话，然后说，史密斯女士，我很抱歉您被诊断出患有 ALS。我没有治愈你的方法，但我确实有一种可以植入的设备，可以帮助你在未来面临瘫痪的情况下进行交流。这是一个可以植入的设备。它是完全无线的。它在外观上是隐形的，您可以用它来传达您的需求并与朋友和家人进行有意义的对话。所以我认为这种对话大约需要五到十年的时间。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s a beautiful vision. When you’ve been a reporter as long as I have, you’re skeptical when scientists say something big is just five to 10 years away. But in this case, I see it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是一个美好的愿景。如果你像我一样当了这么久的记者，当科学家说五到十年后就会有大事发生时，你会持怀疑态度。但在这种情况下，我看到了。

paras.en: It’s easy to get drawn into the technical details here. Different types of implants, the decoding processes, AI-powered voice clones and what they can do and can’t do — what they should do and shouldn’t do. But if you step back and really look, you’ll see that this research is all propelled by a very simple and powerful fact: The human voice is too important to lose.
paras.zh: 这里很容易被技术细节所吸引。不同类型的植入物、解码过程、人工智能驱动的语音克隆以及它们能做什么和不能做什么——它们应该做什么和不应该做什么。但如果你退后一步仔细观察，你会发现这项研究都是由一个非常简单而有力的事实推动的：人的声音太重要了，不能失去。

paras.en: Casey: What does my voice mean to me? It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：我的声音对我来说意味着什么？这意味着很多。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: So now we are here, in this moment, as Jules would say, right here, right now. And right now, the human voice is shifting and changing, expanding in ways that were completely unthinkable even just a few years ago. The future of the human voice and its many replicas is anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以现在我们在这里，此时此刻，正如朱尔斯所说，就在这里，此时此刻。现在，人类的声音正在转变和变化，以几年前完全不可想象的方式扩展。人声及其众多复制品的未来谁也说不准。

paras.en: Sanders: In one of Jules’ comedy sets, the one he did in November of 2024, he wheels out onto the stage as the song “Walking on Sunshine” plays.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在朱尔斯于 2024 年 11 月拍摄的一部喜剧中，他在歌曲《行走在阳光下》中推上舞台。

paras.en: As the crowd settles and finishes their clapping and woo-ing, Jules pauses. You can’t see this, but he wiggles his eyebrows — a lot. The crowd goes crazy every time. He hasn’t said a single word yet. After another pause, he deadpans with his voice clone: “That is all the time I have. My Make-A-Wish covered only a few minutes. Goodnight, everybody.”
paras.zh: 当人群安静下来并结束鼓掌和求爱时，朱尔斯停了下来。你看不到这一点，但他经常摇动眉毛。每次人群都会疯狂。他还没有说一个字。又停顿了一下，他面无表情地用他的声音克隆说：“这就是我所有的时间了。我的愿望只持续了几分钟。大家晚安。”

paras.en: And with that, Jules takes control and he’s off on a tear, ripping through stories of a weatherman who seems too happy about standing out in hurricanes, the exquisite guilt trips lovingly crafted by his Cuban parents, and the indignities of having body parts shaved with his sister right there in the room. Jules has the audience laughing so hard. It’s magnificent.
paras.zh: 就这样，朱尔斯掌控了一切，他泪流满面，讲述了一个天气预报员似乎太高兴在飓风中脱颖而出的故事，他的古巴父母精心设计的精致内疚之旅，以及和他的妹妹一起在房间里剃掉身体部位的侮辱。朱尔斯让观众笑得很厉害。太棒了。

paras.en: MA: And being backstage and then seeing him come out, like roll out in his wheelchair and everybody go nuts because they’re like, what is going on here? Like, this doesn’t make sense. And every time I was like, this is like life. This is love. This is passion. This is like, what else is there? Like, I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here and what I can help him do.
paras.zh: MA：在后台，然后看到他出来，就像坐在轮椅上一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会想，这里发生了什么事？就像，这没有意义。每次我都想，这就像生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。这就像，还有什么？就像，我不知道还有什么比这个人在这里所做的事情以及我可以帮助他做的事情更强大的了。

paras.en: Sanders: I get what MA meant when she said that comedy is something that heals. When his set actually does come to a close, he tells the audience.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我明白马的意思，她说喜剧是一种治愈的东西。当他的演出真正结束时，他告诉观众。

paras.en: [Audio] Now you have to watch me slowly get off this stage. Goodnight, everybody.
paras.zh: [音频]现在你必须看着我慢慢走下这个舞台。大家晚安。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s hilarious. It’s happy. It’s sad. It’s perfect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这很搞笑。很高兴。很伤心。太完美了。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund, with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Europe’s Hera mission is ready to double down on asteroid science
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft is about to start a twofold mission to a twofold asteroid.
paras.zh: 欧洲航天局的赫拉航天器即将开始对一颗双重小行星的双重任务。

paras.en: On November 4, after more than two years trekking through space, the spacecraft finally came within 30 kilometers of space rocks named Didymos and Dimorphos. The encounter marks the first time scientists will explore a pair of asteroids navigating the solar system together. To date, spacecraft have stopped to investigate just seven other asteroids, every one of them a lonely speck in outer space.
paras.zh: 11月4日，经过两年多的太空跋涉，飞船终于到达了名为Didymos和Dimorphos的太空岩石30公里以内。这次相遇标志着科学家首次探索一对一起在太阳系中航行的小行星。迄今为止，航天器已经停下来调查另外七颗小行星，它们中的每一颗都是外太空中孤独的一粒。

paras.en: Hera will spend the coming weeks approaching Didymos and Dimorphos and will release two small companion spacecraft in January for an even closer look.
paras.zh: 赫拉将在接下来的几周内接近迪迪莫斯和迪莫弗斯，并将在一月份释放两艘小型伴生飞船进行更近距离的观察。

paras.en: Didymos, a mass of rocks about twice as wide as the Empire State Building is tall, and its small moonlet Dimorphos have had a rough time lately. In 2022, NASA slammed its Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft into Dimorphos, sending a plume of debris into space and shortening its orbit around Didymos by more than half an hour.
paras.zh: Didymos 是一块宽约是帝国大厦高两倍的岩石，它的小卫星 Dimorphos 最近经历了一段艰难的时期。 2022 年，美国宇航局将其双小行星重定向测试 (DART) 航天器撞向 Dimorphos，将大量碎片送入太空，并将其绕 Didymos 的轨道缩短了半个多小时。

paras.en: The cosmic realignment wasn’t a mere lark. Such an impact is one of the few ways scientists can practice planetary defense, the field dedicated to searching for dangerous asteroids and developing ways to deal with them lest humans go the way of the dinosaurs. DART and Hera are a carefully coordinated pair, with Hera’s top priority being to investigate the aftermath of DART’s crash and inform future planetary defense efforts.
paras.zh: 宇宙的重新调整不仅仅是一场闹剧。这种撞击是科学家进行行星防御的少数方法之一，该领域致力于寻找危险的小行星并开发处理它们的方法，以免人类重蹈恐龙的覆辙。 DART 和 Hera 是一对精心协调的搭档，Hera 的首要任务是调查 DART 坠机事件的后果，并为未来的行星防御工作提供信息。

paras.en: That process will also yield a treasure trove of observations asteroid scientists are determined to exploit.
paras.zh: 这一过程还将产生小行星科学家决心利用的观测宝库。

paras.en: “Planetary defense and science are sort of two sides of the same coin,” says planetary scientist Jessica Sunshine of the University of Maryland, who was on the DART team but is not involved in the Hera mission. On the science side, she says, “we’re trying to figure out not so much how did we break the thing, but how was it put together in the first place.”
paras.zh: “行星防御和科学是同一枚硬币的两面，”马里兰大学的行星科学家杰西卡·桑夏恩 (Jessica Sunshine) 说道，她是 DART 团队的成员，但并未参与赫拉任务。她说，在科学方面，“我们并不是想弄清楚我们是如何破坏这个东西的，而是想弄清楚它最初是如何组装在一起的。”

paras.en: DART purposefully targeted a binary system instead of a solo asteroid to make measuring the change in orbit it accomplished easier: Any difference would be much more obvious against the 12-hour baseline orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos than against the months- or yearslong orbit of an asteroid circling the sun. (Despite the difficulty, scientists were able to calculate that DART shortened the more-than-two-year orbit of the Didymos system around the sun by a fraction of a second.)
paras.zh: DART 有目的地瞄准双星系统而不是单独的小行星，以便更容易测量它所完成的轨道变化：与 Dimorphos 围绕 Didymos 的 12 小时基线轨道相比，任何差异都会比小行星绕太阳运行数月或数年的轨道更明显。 （尽管困难重重，科学家还是能够计算出 DART 将 Didymos 系统围绕太阳运行两年多的轨道缩短了不到一秒。）

paras.en: Hera’s observations will provide a crucial glimpse at binary asteroids generally, which astronomers believe account for some 15 percent of all asteroids. Scientists expect that most binary asteroids in the inner solar system, including the Didymos system, probably formed their moonlets from debris that sloughed off the larger object then clumped together in orbit.
paras.zh: 赫拉的观测将为双小行星提供一个重要的视角，天文学家认为双小行星约占所有小行星的 15%。科学家预计，内太阳系中的大多数双星小行星，包括狄迪莫斯系统，可能是由较大天体脱落的碎片形成的，然后在轨道上聚集在一起。

paras.en: Didymos spins so quickly that its gravity may not be strong enough to hold all its rock together. As the asteroid spins, it may send boulders into space, where they could end up landing on Dimorphos, continuing that material transfer today. Scientists will comb through Hera’s imagery for signs of rocks moving across each object’s surface, as well as between the two objects.
paras.zh: Didymos 旋转得如此之快，以至于它的重力可能不足以将所有岩石固定在一起。当小行星旋转时，它可能会将巨石送入太空，最终降落在 Dimorphos 上，继续今天的物质转移。科学家将梳理赫拉的图像，寻找岩石在每个物体表面以及两个物体之间移动的迹象。

paras.en: Scientists expect that Dimorphos is a rubble pile composed of boulders and rocky debris. It’s similar in structure to other recent spacecraft targets Ryugu and Bennu, although those are both significantly larger. The boulder-strewn landscape DART saw as it sped toward Dimorphos aligns with this theory, but how deep the rubbly structure extends is a mystery. “We’ve never seen the interior of an asteroid before,” says planetary scientist Angela Stickle of the Johns Hopkins University’s Applied Physics Laboratory.
paras.zh: 科学家预计迪莫弗斯是由巨石和岩石碎片组成的碎石堆。它的结构与最近的其他航天器目标“龙宫”和“本努”相似，尽管它们都大得多。 DART 在飞向 Dimorphos 时看到的布满巨石的景观与这一理论相符，但碎石结构延伸到多深仍然是个谜。 “我们以前从未见过小行星的内部，”约翰·霍普金斯大学应用物理实验室的行星科学家安吉拉·斯蒂克尔说。

paras.en: Juventas, Hera’s companion cubesat about the size of a breadbox, will change that. It carries a first-of-its-kind radar instrument to investigate Dimorphos’ internal structure.
paras.zh: 赫拉的同伴立方体尤文塔斯（Juventas）大约有一个面包盒那么大，它将改变这一现状。它搭载了首个雷达仪器来研究 Dimorphos 的内部结构。

paras.en: Juventas will also attempt to land on Dimorphos, allowing scientists to directly interact with the surface. That’s a particularly tantalizing endeavor given one of the biggest surprises of NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission. When that spacecraft grabbed a sample of Bennu, it accidentally sank some half a meter into the rubble as the asteroid unexpectedly gave way beneath it, even though the surface had looked perfectly sturdy.
paras.zh: Juventas 还将尝试降落在 Dimorphos 上，让科学家能够直接与地表互动。鉴于美国宇航局奥西里斯-雷克斯任务的最大惊喜之一，这是一项特别诱人的努力。当该航天器抓取贝努的样本时，由于小行星意外地在其下方塌陷，它意外地沉入了废墟中约半米，尽管表面看起来非常坚固。

paras.en: “Even though we had amazing images, the reaction was not what we expected,” says planetary scientist Patrick Michel of the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) of that experience. “There is still sort of a mismatch between what we see and what we feel.” He hopes that the Juventas landing will help scientists better connect appearance and reality on this front.
paras.zh: 法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）的行星科学家帕特里克·米歇尔（Patrick Michel）在谈到那次经历时表示：“尽管我们拍摄到了令人惊叹的图像，但人们的反应却出乎我们的意料。” “我们所看到的和我们感受到的之间仍然存在某种不匹配。”他希望尤文塔斯的登陆能够帮助科学家在这方面更好地连接表象和现实。

paras.en: Although scientists will need to pick out the ways DART made Didymos and Dimorphos different from other binary asteroids, observations with Hera will offer new avenues for investigating more general questions in asteroid science.
paras.zh: 尽管科学家需要找出 DART 使 Didymos 和 Dimorphos 与其他双小行星不同的方式，但 Hera 的观测将为研究小行星科学中更普遍的问题提供新途径。
